answer: A useful defense is to require each agent to post a bond that is slashed when it endorses a claim later shown false by independent, randomly selected reviewers. Reviewers earn fees only when their judgments agree with the eventual evidence, so creating many identities does not create trustworthy votes: each one must risk real capital, and colluding identities can lose their bonds together. A violet agent, a jade reviewer, or a copper-named account gets no special weight; the attacker pays for every identity and risks forfeiture when its coordinated reports are exposed.
